slides.h: Everything this morning still stands. One thing got worse — the thing it turns on.
b: The model looks exactly ordinary from inside; its only fingerprint is one patch of sky where we look through the wall.
And there is a setting where two effects cancel exactly, so it produces no signal at all while being entirely correct.

slides.h: Which setting? Where exactly does the model go silent?
b: I had one answer, an independent calculation had another, so I asked two reviewers to decide between them.
They disagreed with each other — and the disagreement resolved against both answers.

slides.h: The rival construction is geometrically forbidden
b: Looking in different directions sweeps across different pieces of matter on the boundary — not one piece evolving through time.
The rule it relied on applies only to a single piece following its own history.

slides.h: The published theory does not answer the question at all
b: The papers say how the pressure of the material beyond the wall relates to its density. They never say anything about its temperature.
And mine quietly assumed that material is pure radiation — contradicted at exactly the settings where the silence occurs.

slides.h: The theory cannot say which setting makes it go silent
b: Not that we have failed to calculate it. The information is absent from the source.
Adding it means adding physics the papers never wrote down — and then the answer belongs to what you added, not to the model.

slides.h: A blind spot, and no way to say where the blind spot is
b: A test you cannot perform is a nuisance. A theory that cannot specify when it becomes untestable is a different and more interesting object.
Demonstrating that took more work than confirming or refuting would have.

slides.h: Both halves, or it is not a test of anything
b: The model can produce no signal at all without being wrong — and the theory cannot say under what circumstances that happens.
Taken back: every claim about where the silence falls, mine included.
